{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVdzeZs8AAAABbhLL1w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpi2wzhFFcns", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpi2w", "number": 9, "title": "Add selectable MMD (Animasa Miku) glTF character with MotionBricks retargeting and MMD physics", "body": "## Goal

Extend the existing [MotionBricks SOMA keyboard locomotion MVP](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/issues/5) so that users can **select either the current native SOMA character or a classic MMD character** (preferably the **Animasa/あにまさ式 Hatsune Miku** used historically in Three.js MMD examples). Both should move using the **same MotionBricks-generated SOMA motion**, while the MMD character **retains MMD-style appearance and working MMD rigid-body/joint physics** (hair, clothing, etc.).

**Important:** MMD assets must be **converted to glTF/GLB at development/build time** and loaded with **GLTFLoader and MMD-specific glTF extension plugins**. Do **not** load PMD/PMX directly in the shipped demo.

## Primary references

- [takahirox/mmd-gltf](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf): PMX → glTF conversion, toon/outline, SDEF/QDEF, MMD IK/append, physics extension and GLTFLoader plugin patterns. In particular:
  - [Conversion & plugins](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/pipeline.md)
  - [Rigid-body physics extension/runtime](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/physics.md)
- [takahirox/three-mmd-loader](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader) (package `@takahirox/three-mmd`): reference MMD animation, IK/physics/renderer behavior, *not* a requirement to load PMD/PMX at runtime.
- [takahirox/MMDLoader-app](https://github.com/takahirox/MMDLoader-app) and [historical interactive demo](https://github.com/takahirox/MMDLoader-app/blob/master/app_interactive.html), which referenced the classic `miku_v2.pmd` in Three.js r87.
- [MotionBricks SOMA ONNX model and runtime](https://github.com/NVlabs/motionbricks).

## Work items

### 1. Character/model selection and assets

- [ ] Add a simple **Character** selector: `SOMA` (the current native character; default) / `MMD (Animasa Miku)` (or the precise verified character name).
- [ ] Locate and verify the provenance/author of the old Three.js Miku asset (`miku_v2.pmd`) and confirm whether it is the intended あにまさ式. **Do not assume the name or redistribution rights.** Check creator terms, Crypton/Piapro character-use guidelines, requirements for conversion/derivatives, attribution and public GitHub Pages hosting. If bundling/rehosting is not authorized, document the blocker and propose a compliant acquisition/runtime asset flow or an equivalent properly licensed MMD demo model; do not silently substitute or publish unlicensed assets.
- [ ] Produce a reproducible, documented **offline PMD/PMX → glTF/GLB** pipeline with skinned mesh, skeleton, texture/material, morph and relevant MMD metadata retained. `takahirox/mmd-gltf` currently focuses on PMX; if choosing a PMD source, explicitly handle and validate **PMD → PMX** or add a supported conversion path (preserving physics and bone identity). Don't use a static-pose-only export.
- [ ] Preserve MMD appearance via the available glTF toon/outline/material extensions and register corresponding `GLTFLoader` plugins. Evaluate the optional SDEF/QDEF plugins according to the chosen source asset; document fallbacks and visual differences.
- [ ] Use only glTF/GLB and required runtime assets on the deployed page (not source PMD/PMX). Respect asset licenses and third-party notices.

### 2. MotionBricks SOMA → MMD retargeting

- [ ] Reuse the existing keyboard input, target generation, ONNX inference and continuous SOMA motion playback; **do not add a second motion model or replace generation with prerecorded VMD**.
- [ ] Implement a documented, testable **SOMA joint → MMD bone mapping** for the selected character. The implementation owner should design the mapping and account for center/groove/waist/root motion, rest/bind poses, local/world bone axes, handedness, scaling, parent hierarchies, twist/extra bones and toes.
- [ ] Preserve coherent walk/run/turn/stop transitions with root motion, facing and ground alignment; avoid obvious flipping, floating or snapping.
- [ ] Keep the native SOMA model behavior unchanged, and structure the retargeter so more MMD models could be supported in the future.

### 3. MMD physics and IK integration

- [ ] **Enable and visibly demonstrate MMD physics**, carried through the converted glTF via MMD-specific extension metadata and applied at runtime (e.g. the `MMD_physics` / `MMDPhysicsPlugin` / `PhysicsRig` approach in `takahirox/mmd-gltf`, if it covers the selected model). Ensure rigid-body/joint data and necessary runtime are preserved; mere glTF skinning is not sufficient.
- [ ] Define and test the per-frame ordering/ownership explicitly: **MotionBricks SOMA pose → retargeted MMD driving bones → optional IK/append processing → physics step → final bone transforms/skin render**. Handle physics reset and model switching, avoid applying solver/physics twice, prevent excessive jitter and resource leaks. Decide which bones physics can override vs follow.
- [ ] **Choose MMD IK on/off experimentally**; do not hardcode a decision before checking the retargeted leg/foot pose. Direct FK from SOMA may justify IK off. If driving MMD foot IK target bones gives better stance/ground contact, enable the required chains. Compare feet during walking, running, stopping and turns, and **document why**. IK should not fight the retargeted FK pose or physics.
- [ ] Prefer retaining MMD-specific appearance/behavior (toon/outline, springy hair/clothes, append/grant where needed), while prioritizing a reliable working demo over bit-identical MMD reproduction. Document unsupported features.

### 4. UI, deployment, validation

- [ ] Switching between SOMA and MMD should preserve existing keyboard controls and demo behavior. Reset/rebind physics and motion state safely; no dangling workers or duplicated physics stepping; handle loading and errors gracefully.
- [ ] Keep Three.js WebGPU rendering supported and GitHub Pages static deployment functional; check extension plugins, Ammo/WASM/worker asset URLs and the `/three-motionbricks/` base path.
- [ ] Add regression tests for mapping/rest-pose transforms and model switching, plus browser smoke tests for visible MMD physics response and walk/run/turn/stop.
- [ ] Update README / asset provenance, licenses, conversion steps, plugin dependencies and known limitations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can select **SOMA** and **MMD** on the same demo page.
- [ ] SOMA continues to work as before, and the MMD character is **a converted glTF/GLB loaded through registered MMD-aware GLTFLoader plugins** (not direct PMD/PMX loading).
- [ ] In MMD mode, **actual MotionBricks-generated** walking/running/turning/stopping drives the character using a correct SOMA → MMD retargeter.
- [ ] The MMD model looks recognizably MMD (toon/outline as supported) and **MMD rigid-body physics visibly reacts during MotionBricks locomotion** (hair/clothing/appropriate dynamic parts), without gross instability.
- [ ] IK choice (on/off or selective) and the bone mapping rationale, limitations and verification are recorded.
- [ ] Asset provenance and permission for **public redistribution/hosting of the converted character** are verified and documented; if permission cannot be established, do not publish it without permission and clearly record the blocker.
- [ ] Production build and tests pass; Pages deployment continues to work, with no broken glTF/texture/extension/physics runtime URLs.

## Implementation discretion

Please choose the correct mapping, IK strategy and detailed integration approach based on observed behavior; they are deliberately **not prespecified** in this issue. Focus on a reusable retargeting layer and clear test evidence, not a hardcoded one-off pose copy.
